title: Why is the B3LYP/6-31G* Level of Theory so Successful?

import.label: ⬇ Import my def2-TZVP energies from Experiments 4 and 5

options: d-type polarization functions on the non-hydrogen atoms
An extra s function on hydrogen
quiz.explain: 6-31G* (also written 6-31G(d)) adds one set of d functions to every non-hydrogen atom, letting the electron density polarize in bonds.

quiz.q: 6-31G*, def2-SVP, cc-pVDZ and pc-1 are all…
quiz.explain: All four use two functions per valence orbital plus polarization functions, but they were optimized in different ways, so their sizes and behavior differ.

quiz.q: If a small basis gives a *smaller* error than a large basis with the same functional, the most likely explanation is…
options: the small basis is more accurate
a fortuitous cancellation between the basis-set error and the functional's own error
the large basis set is broken
quiz.explain: The basis-set error and the functional error have different origins. When they happen to have opposite signs they cancel, which is luck, not accuracy, and it won't transfer to other problems.
